purpose: every refusal validate.py makes of a world file, as data: the set it scans, the condition each record must meet, and the message; validate.py derives the records and one generic runner judges them, and mutations.json holds one broken copy per rule that must trip it
ops: empty, nonempty, is_true, is_false, eq_value, when (if, then), all

rules.message: no *.world.json under the worlds directory, so nothing below was checked
{world}: is not JSON: {parse_error}
{world}: does not match world.schema.json: {schema_errors}
{world} {where}: is not in the expression grammar: {syntax_errors}
{world} {where}: uses a word the world does not declare: {unknown_words}
{world} {where}: units or types do not agree: {unit_errors}
{world} {where}: exceeds the node or depth bound, so its evaluation cost is not bounded by the world: {bound_errors}
{world}: equations, scores or agents refer to each other in a cycle, which would never finish evaluating: {cycle}
{world}: the seed the world ships with breaks its own rules: {seed_error}
{world} rule {id}: refuses without saying why; a require rule needs a message
{world} rule {id}: applies to types or tags the world does not declare: {unknown_targets}
{world} action {verb}: emits no events, so taking it would change nothing in the log
{world} link to {parent}: dangles: {problems}
{world} link to {parent}: the grid covers {extent_sq_ft} sq ft, more than the {parent_extent_sq_ft} sq ft of the parcel it links to
{world} {where}: a binding outcome reads projected_support(); an agent's assumed vote is a projection and never binding
{world} {type}.{property}: a {kind} figure needs a twin id, a row id, or a placeholder with its reason
{world} type {type}: sprite {sprite} is neither generic nor a declared extension
{world} type {type}: footprint {footprint} tiles, but footprint_mm spans {derived} tiles of this grid (ceil of footprint_mm / (tile_ft x 304.8))
{world} instance {id}: two seed instances share this id, so one would overwrite the other
{world} instance {id}: a measured instance needs a source: a twin id, a row id, a file or a stated tag
{world} instance {id}: a measured instance needs an error object; missing {missing_error_fields}
{world} instance {id}: error {unreasoned} must be a number with a source or null with a null_reason
